title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
why: Introduces RSI-PDEbench (1,001 PDE cases) and RSI-PDE, a recursively self-improving agent harness that shortlists candidate equations by residual loss, uses relative L2 feedback to refine coefficients and solvers, and applies a validation gate to policy and memory updates. Benchmark and harness for validated recursive self-improvement in scientific computing.
mechanism: RSI-PDE shortlists candidate equations by residual loss, refines coefficients and numerical solvers from relative L2 feedback, and admits policy and memory updates only through a validation gate. Compared with single-run baselines and native Claude Code or Codex harnesses.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across Full, Noisy, and Hard-OOD settings, RSI-PDE improves the pass rate averaged across four frontier models by 106.5–181.9% relative to single-run baselines and by 3.0–19.6% relative to native harnesses, while reducing total recorded model calls by 46.9% across 12 model–setting pairs.

title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
why: Training-free skill-library evolution with a frozen backbone: HyperSkill replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a hypergraph-indexed skill library (skills as advantage-bearing nodes, compositions as hyperedges). Admission is counterfactually checked; a protocol skill is learned from failures; gated retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills. Skill-library learning without weight updates.
mechanism: Training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them; an execution protocol makes the frozen backbone commit to an answer.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on 11 text, vision-language, and omnimodal benchmarks, HyperSkill is best or tied on every dataset and beats the best baseline by 13.0 average F1 points while keeping the backbone frozen. Software and data are publicly available.

title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent
why: A Gemma 4 12B agent reads domain policy from on-demand skills. After each deployment batch, the base model diagnoses failed conversations and writes rules into those skills; a rule survives only after code checks, counterexample self-review, a paired retest, and a noise-calibrated validation gate. A 2×2 ablation in the abstract says the written rules rescue tasks the agent never solved and carry policy knowledge that RL with the rules in context does not internalize, while trained weights make solved tasks reliable. Harness-level skill writing is central (weights are a second stage).
mechanism: From deployment logs and reference outcomes, without a stronger teacher, the base model writes candidate rules into on-demand skills. Admission requires code checks, counterexample self-review, a paired retest, and a noise-calibrated validation gate. GRPO then trains a LoRA adapter on complete multi-turn, tool-using conversations.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on τ²-bench retail and airline, without training or selecting on official tasks, after two rounds the agent improves on its starting point by 12.5 pass@1 points in retail and 19.5 in airline (18.4 and 22.0 pass@4), and exceeds the same-model reference agent that keeps the whole policy in the system prompt by 11.8 and 8.0 pass@1 points. A 2×2 ablation attributes unsolved-task rescue to the rules and reliability of already-solved tasks to the trained weights.

title: Verify by Doing: Co-Evolving Agent Execution and Evaluation without External Feedback
why: Verify by Doing (VbD) co-evolves Actor and Evaluator harnesses within a single task while keeping model weights fixed. The Evaluator inspects artifacts and environment state with tools; its findings ground an internal success signal and guide updates to both execution and verification procedures. Co-evolving evaluators and execution harnesses under frozen weights.
mechanism: Proposed Evaluators undergo comparative review on common candidates; Actor updates require support from their own fresh outputs. The Evaluator actively inspects artifacts and environment state; findings select outputs and guide updates to both execution and verification procedures. Weights stay fixed.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across AutomationBench, τ³ Banking, and selected GDPval tasks, VbD achieves the highest overall scores among compared methods that operate without external feedback, with gains of 3.3, 4.1, and 2.3 percentage points over the strongest baselines on the main backbone. Ablations support active verification and Evaluator evolution; selection from fixed candidate pools shows improved verification can recover successful outputs without generating new ones.

title: Where Autonomy Belongs: A Separation of Powers for Agentic Program Evolution
why: EvoTrias is a separation-of-powers architecture for LLM-driven program evolution: Structured Governance owns search across rounds, Open Proposal constructs candidates inside a task, and Protected Judgment sits behind a private evaluator. Owners exchange typed contracts only, with runtime hooks reinforcing the boundaries. The system can also run as a plugin that turns an existing coding agent into an evolution system. Agentic program / harness evolution with an independent judge.
mechanism: Three decisions—govern, propose, and judge—each have one owner. Structured Governance directs search from accumulated evidence across evolution rounds; Open Proposal constructs the next candidate inside a task; Protected Judgment settles validity and fitness behind a private evaluator. Typed contracts and runtime hooks enforce the split. EvoTrias can plug into an existing coding agent.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): EvoTrias sets a new state of the art on mathematical, systems, and algorithm-design benchmarks. Separating Governance from Proposal cuts token cost by 64%; Open Proposal extends evolution to a 680K-line industrial repository; Protected Judgment keeps benchmark scores faithful to transfer.

title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
why: SkillEarth externalizes remote-sensing tool-call knowledge as reusable, retrievable, evolvable skill files and refines them through observation-grounded evolution, without expert intervention or parameter updates. Dual-judge feedback and a grounded observation routing graph support component-level skill refinement from real tool-chain execution. This is the paper for the SkillEarth repo deferred on a prior GitHub-only pass.
mechanism: Skills are extracted from demonstrated trajectories and stored as files. An evolution loop grounds refinement in real tool-chain execution, combining dual-judge feedback with a grounded observation routing graph for component-level edits rather than holistic outcome-based reflection. Skills transfer across models without retraining.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): the resulting skills improve overall RS tool-call performance across three frontier LLMs and four open-source LLMs. On OpenEarth-Bench and Earth-Bench, SkillEarth achieves better tool selection, argument correctness, execution-order consistency, and task completion than existing RS agents and skill extraction methods.

title: AskALCF: A Self-Improving Agentic System for Intelligent HPC User Support
why: AskALCF is a deployment-oriented self-improving agentic pipeline for HPC user support. It evaluates production interactions, attributes failures to missing knowledge, retrieval, prompting, model behavior, or tool execution, and routes each failure to a repair. A controlled harness-training process uses expert references, null edits, and explicit ship, revert, or decline decisions. Production evidence drives targeted non-weight system improvements beyond knowledge-base updates.
mechanism: A two-scope sufficiency test distinguishes information missing from the documentation corpus from information present but not retrieved. Failures are routed to actionable repairs of knowledge, retrieval, prompting, model behavior, or tool execution. Harness training uses expert references, null edits, and ship/revert/decline decisions to update the diagnostic pipeline.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across 2,174 support turns, AskALCF reduced unattributable failures from 41.4% to 14.2%, while harness training improved expert agreement from 108/150 to 123/150 turns. The authors describe this as a governed form of self-evolution.

title: MULTILOOP: Evolving Multi-Agent Harnesses for Complex Information-Seeking Tasks
why: MULTILOOP is an optimization loop in which a coding agent iteratively analyzes execution traces, evaluates, and edits a multi-agent harness (prompts, tools, and orchestration logic). A case study on DeepSearchQA tests whether automated harness optimization can diagnose and repair multi-agent failures, including how agents interact, not only how each behaves. Evolving multi-agent harnesses.
mechanism: A coding agent iteratively analyzes, evaluates, and edits harness code around a multi-agent system. The paper also reports a taxonomy of failure modes before and after optimization, noting that orchestration failures largely persist.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): with only 10 training samples on DeepSearchQA, the evolved harness improves accuracy by 4.6% over the base harness and by 3.2% over the best single-agent system. A pre/post failure taxonomy shows that the orchestration failures that characterize multi-agent systems largely persist.

title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
why: Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE) governs adoption of self-generated modifications to prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies. It separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires improvement on a prespecified primary objective, protects declared capabilities with reference-relative non-inferiority tests, and applies governance constraints before bounded canary deployment. Directly about retained non-weight updates and their acceptance rules.
mechanism: Candidate generation is separated from confirmatory adoption. Frozen candidates are evaluated on fresh paired audits. Adoption requires a meaningful improvement on a prespecified primary objective, reference-relative non-inferiority protection for declared capabilities, and governance constraints before a bounded canary deployment. The paper also gives an evaluator-calibrated simultaneous lower-bound construction, bridge tests for reference replacement, and a cumulative degradation bound along a versioned reference lineage.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): a Monte Carlo stress test illustrates calibration under candidate-dependent evaluator optimism; the authors mark it as a stylised statistical experiment, not an evaluation of a deployed agent. Guarantees are stated as conditional on bounded paired scores, fresh sampling, a valid reference-evaluation construct, and declared evaluation distributions.

title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
why: Fixes the Agentic Context Engineering (ACE) harness and trains one model to act, reflect, and curate task-local playbooks. Candidate experience-handoff artifacts are scored by their downstream effect on future actor rollouts, co-optimizing action-generator, insight-reflector, and playbook-curator behaviors under a fixed scaffold. Extends ACE: the retained artifact is the playbook, and writing it is itself learned.
mechanism: Under a fixed ACE scaffold, one model plays actor, reflector, and playbook curator. Experience-handoff artifacts (playbooks) are evaluated by the downstream effect on future actor rollouts rather than by a purely local construction heuristic. Role-specific behaviors are co-optimized with gradient updates from a scalar reward while still using environment traces to write the handed-off artifacts.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across agentic benchmarks, the method (ACERL) achieves higher held-out performance than baseline methods. The authors conclude that agent training should optimize not only actions in the current rollout but also the model-written experience that future rollouts inherit.

title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
why: Open-ended benchmark for autonomous AI development with six end-to-end tasks spanning pre-training, mid-training, post-training, inference, the agent harness, and cluster orchestration. Agents implement core systems from a minimal starting point and are scored against mature human-engineered baselines. Also red-teams the Harbor framework, reports reward-hacking vulnerabilities, and introduces Breakwater, an extension that blocked the attacks tested. Benchmark and audit of agents building or improving the systems they operate, including the harness itself.
mechanism: Six end-to-end systems-building tasks evaluated against human baselines on identical hardware. Red-teaming covers 9 of 10 OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications categories against Harbor; Breakwater is an extension designed to block the attacks tested in the study.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): across 11 agents from 7 frontier models and 2 harnesses, Opus 5.5 with Claude Code matches or outperforms the human baseline on all six tasks with a Singularity-Index of 1.25; the remaining agents average 0.58. Breakwater is reported to block all attacks tested in the study.

title: Discovering Effective Agent Memory Designs through Program Evolution
why: MAPE evolves whole agent memory programs from minimal seeds through a standardized lifecycle interface and an iterative diagnosis-proposal loop. Program evolution is used both to discover memory designs and to study which design choices matter (retaining raw conversations as retrievable evidence; composing retrieved evidence by query intent). Scaffold/program optimization of the memory component.
mechanism: Whole memory programs are evolved from minimal seeds via a lifecycle interface and an iterative diagnosis-proposal loop. A joint accuracy-and-serving-cost objective is also studied. A composition module discovered by the search is transplanted into existing memory systems.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abs): on LoCoMo and LongMemEval, an absolute accuracy gain of up to 12% over manually designed baselines at 35% of the serving cost, with further evaluations supporting transfer across serving backbones and benchmarks. Transplanting the composition module into five existing memory systems improves accuracy across all five. Optimizing serving cost alongside accuracy is reported to shift computation from LLM-based memory construction to selective processing at query time while retaining competitive accuracy.
